Consult Summary:
- A likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection presenting with dysuria, foul-smelling urine, visible blood in urine, and midline lower abdominal pain; a 3-day antibiotic course with supportive measures was planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination with an unpleasant smell and blood-tinged urine for six days; lower abdominal (midline) pain.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began six days ago and are ongoing; pain described as 7/10 and comes and goes.
- Symptoms and findings:
  - Dysuria with burning on urination.
  - Hematuria (blood in urine) described as spotting.
  - Lower abdominal pain in the middle; no loin pain.
  - No fever or temperature elevation.
  - Urination is possible; no reported inability to void.
  - Appetite and oral intake preserved.
  - No vaginal discharge reported.
- Exposures and factors: No dehydration, no excessive exercise, no recent sexual activity contributing to symptoms reported.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg taken orally, three times daily.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.
- Social history: Lives with friends; works as a support worker; drinks alcohol occasionally (about one glass of wine per week); non-smoker.
- Family history: None reported.
- Review of systems: No fever, no back/loin pain, no weight loss reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Probable urinary tract infection (cystitis) with dysuria, midline lower abdominal pain, and hematuria; afebrile.
  - Plan:
    - Initiate a 3-day course of antibiotics; prescription to Knightsbridge Practice; pick up in about an hour.
      - Antibiotic name not provided in the transcript.
    - Advise high fluid intake: 2.5–3 liters of water per day.
    - Consider cranberry juice intake and urine-acidity sachets (from chemist) to help urine acidity.
    - No urine test required at this time; treat empirically.
    - Monitor for worsening symptoms or new fever; seek re-evaluation if symptoms worsen, fever develops, or there are any problems passing urine.
    - If infections become recurrent, discuss further management.
    - Thermometer at home: patient advised to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.
    - Return visit not required if symptoms improve; contact if not resolving or worsening.

General Plan:
- Ensure prescription is sent to the patient’s chosen pharmacy; pickup approximately within an hour to lunchtime.
- Instruct patient to start antibiotics promptly after pickup.
- Provide supportive measures as listed (hydration, cranberry juice, urine acidity sachets).
- Reassess if symptoms worsen or recur; consider further evaluation if recurrent UTIs occur.
